candidate.title: Nextera Library Preparation
candidate.scope: The single Illumina Nextera Library Preparation schematic: transposase engagement with DNA, tagmentation, the depicted end-labelled amplification intermediate, and amplification to a product ready for cluster generation. No kit version or alternative workflow is identified. The biological material represented is input DNA; the library carries fragments of that DNA between synthetic terminal elements. Cluster generation and sequencing are downstream interfaces, not depicted operations.

states.label: DNA
features: A long blue double line depicts double-stranded input DNA.
The specimen, genomic origin and biological target subset are unspecified.

evidence.locator: Upper DNA double line and DNA label

states.label: Transposase with coloured DNA-end elements
features: Two blue protein icons labelled Transposase carry magenta or green arms.
The coloured arms are interpreted as DNA tags because the same colours subsequently appear at fragment ends; their sequences and chemical end groups are unspecified.
Transposase is the catalytic component, not the biological target or final readout carrier.

evidence.locator: Top pair of protein icons, coloured arms and Transposase label
Coloured arms on top transposases compared with coloured ends after Tagmentation
evidence.rationale: Magenta and green elements move from the protein-associated icons to the blue DNA ends across the tagmentation sequence, supporting interpretation as transferred end tags.

states.label: DNA engaged by transposase complexes
features: The blue DNA remains a continuous double line in the second row.
Magenta-bearing and green-bearing transposase icons contact it at two separated positions.

evidence.locator: Second DNA row below the first downward arrow

states.label: Tagmented DNA fragments
features: The previously continuous blue DNA is interrupted at two positions, with magenta and green segments at the new boundaries.
A central double-stranded fragment is labelled approximately 300 bp and has a magenta left end and green right end.

Short flanking DNA segments are also drawn. The next row follows a representative fragment with both coloured ends; no selection, disposal or separate downstream processing of the flanking segments is shown.
The approximately 300 bp annotation is on the tagmented central fragment, not on the final P5/P7-bearing product.

evidence.locator: Fragmented DNA row with ~300bp annotation, coloured boundaries and flanking segments

states.label: P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 amplification oligonucleotides
features: The amplification intermediate depicts a left arm labelled P5 and Index 2 and a right arm labelled Index 1 and P7.
These arms are interpreted as tailed amplification primers associated with the magenta and green end tags, respectively; isolated free primers are not separately drawn.
No index sequences, index-to-sample assignments or primer nucleotide sequences are supplied.

evidence.locator: Slanted left P5/Index 2 arm and right Index 1/P7 arm on the pre-amplification fragment
evidence.rationale: The arms meet the coloured terminal duplex elements and their labels reappear as continuous terminal segments after the Amplification arrow, supporting the tailed-primer interpretation without specifying primer chemistry.

states.label: End-tagged DNA fragment with labelled amplification arms
features: A blue double-stranded insert is bordered by magenta left and green right end elements.
The left arm extends outward through Index 2 toward P5; the right arm extends outward through Index 1 toward P7.
The slanted arms preserve the visible partially duplex/overhanging representation; the diagram does not specify chemical end groups or a gap-repair mechanism.

evidence.locator: Intermediate between the ~300bp fragment row and the Amplification arrow

states.label: Product ready for cluster generation
features: The final schematic is a single linear representation ordered left to right as P5, Index 2, a blue DNA insert, Index 1 and P7.
The single-line cartoon does not by itself establish the final product's strand state.
Both index-labelled regions and the terminal P5/P7 elements are physically connected to the DNA insert in the final representation.
The product is explicitly ready for cluster generation; no clusters, sequencing reads or analysis results are depicted.

evidence.locator: Bottom linear construct and Product ready for cluster generation label

operations.label: Transposase engagement with DNA (unlabelled arrow)
operations.description: The initially separate transposase complexes become associated with two positions on the continuous DNA substrate. The output differs by protein/tag attachment, while DNA fragmentation is depicted only in the next transition.
operations.mechanism: Protein-DNA engagement is depicted. Transposase is a catalyst carrying end-tag elements; this association does not imply chemical consumption of the protein.
operations.information_effect: The input DNA remains continuous at this boundary; no index-labelled elements are yet shown on the DNA.

evidence.locator: First downward arrow linking free protein icons above DNA to protein icons contacting the second DNA row

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: The engaged continuous DNA becomes shorter DNA fragments with coloured end elements. The central illustrated fragment is approximately 300 bp, with different coloured tags at its two ends. Flanking segments remain visible in the same output row.
operations.mechanism: At schematic resolution, transposase-associated cleavage and end tagging are combined in the transition labelled Tagmentation. The drawing does not resolve individual catalytic intermediates or the enzyme's subsequent fate.
operations.information_effect: The blue DNA fragments retain local segments of the input DNA sequence as the future insert carrier. Fragmentation breaks the original long-molecule continuity, while the coloured end tags provide the depicted interface to subsequent amplification arms.

evidence.locator: Second downward arrow, Tagmentation label, continuous protein-bound DNA above and broken tagged DNA below
Blue DNA continuity and coloured end elements before and after Tagmentation
evidence.rationale: The same blue duplex is drawn as shorter pieces after the arrow, and the protein-associated colours appear at the breaks. This supports fragmentation plus end tagging and preservation of target-derived inserts, but not a specific enzyme identity or bond-level mechanism.

operations.label: Association of labelled amplification arms (unlabelled arrow)
operations.description: The next downward arrow follows a representative end-tagged DNA fragment into an intermediate with P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 arms at opposite ends. Interpreting these arms as amplification primers, the output differs by their association with the end-tagged insert. This is an illustrative continuation of one fragment type, not a depicted size-selection or purification operation.
operations.information_effect: The depicted left and right interfaces associate the same DNA insert with the two index-labelled and P5/P7-bearing arms. Their completed incorporation is shown after Amplification.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from the ~300bp tagged-fragment row to the P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 intermediate
Coloured terminal duplex elements, slanted labelled arms and the subsequent Amplification arrow
evidence.rationale: The correspondence between end-tag colours, attached arms and final continuous labelled ends supports primer association as the local interface. No separate annealing conditions, repair step or selection is supplied.

operations.label: Amplification
operations.description: The end-labelled DNA intermediate is amplified to a library construct with continuous terminal P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 regions around the blue insert. The resulting product is labelled ready for cluster generation.
operations.mechanism: Amplification is explicitly named. The figure does not specify a polymerase, cycling scheme or internal extension/repair sequence.
operations.information_effect: The final library carries target-derived DNA inserts linked to two index-labelled regions and the P5/P7 terminal interface. Interpreting the blue insert as retained input sequence, subsequent insert sequencing could report sampled input-DNA sequence; this diagram supplies neither an actual sequencing measurement nor evidence of complete or unbiased target representation.

evidence.locator: Final downward arrow beside Amplification and bottom Product ready for cluster generation construct
Blue insert retained through the tagmented fragment, amplification intermediate and final construct
evidence.rationale: The repeated blue insert between the coloured ends supports a target-derived DNA carrier through library preparation. Sequence recovery is a downstream interpretation of that retained insert, rather than a depicted readout or a claim about coverage.
